name: Integer Coercion Error
principle: Code casts, promotes, extends, or truncates an integer so the stored value no longer matches the intended value. The wrong value can bypass checks and then drive allocation sizes, copy lengths, indexes, or loop bounds.
detection_signals: signed int/short/char assigned to size_t or unsigned and later used as malloc/calloc/realloc size
negative-capable signed length checked only with len > MAX before conversion to size_t/unsigned
int or long assigned to short/char/byte without range check before use as length/count/index
function call passes signed variable to size_t parameter of memcpy/memmove/strncpy/read/fread
packet/file/network count field parsed into signed integer then multiplied by sizeof(...) for allocation
explicit cast like (unsigned)len or (size_t)len on untrusted or range-unchecked value
Java narrowing cast like (short)i or (byte)i on untrusted value before array allocation/indexing
negative_signals: range check enforces 0 <= len && len <= MAX before any cast to size_t/unsigned
checked conversion helper rejects out-of-range values before assignment to narrower type
same validated variable and same integer type are used for both bounds check and sink
C++ std::in_range<T>(x) or equivalent guard precedes static_cast<T>(x)
Java Math.toIntExact or explicit min/max check precedes narrowing conversion
false_defense_traps: checking only len > MAX misses negative signed values
checking before narrowing cast does not prove the narrowed value is unchanged
explicit casts silence compiler warnings but do not validate range
using strncpy/memcpy with a coerced length still overflows if the length changed
null-terminating after a copy does not fix an oversized copy length
verification_focus: Does any integer cast, promotion, extension, or truncation change an untrusted value before it is used in a size, index, count, allocation, copy, or loop sink?

consequence_chains.trigger: negative signed value is converted to unsigned or size_t
consequence_chains.consequence: huge length causes resource exhaustion or oversized copy

consequence_chains.trigger: coerced length bypasses a bounds check and reaches a buffer operation
consequence_chains.consequence: buffer overflow and possible code execution

consequence_chains.trigger: coerced return value or length prevents error handling and controls a write offset/size

patch_principle: Avoid unnecessary casts and mixed signedness for sizes, counts, and indexes.
Validate both minimum and maximum bounds before conversion.
Perform the security check in the exact type used by the sink.
Reject values that cannot be represented in the destination type before narrowing.
Use checked conversion APIs or languages/settings that trap ambiguous casts.

minimal_examples.vuln: int n = packet->headers; if (n > 100) error(); headers = malloc(n * sizeof(PacketHeader));
minimal_examples.safe: int n = packet->headers; if (n < 0 || n > 100) error(); headers = malloc((size_t)n * sizeof(PacketHeader));
